title: Pennsylvania Home EV Charger Rebates 2026: What Ended and What to Ask
desc: Pennsylvania home EV charger incentives in 2026: the federal 30C credit ended June 30, 2026, and we found no home charger rebate from PECO or PPL Electric. How to price an install anyway.
h1: Pennsylvania Home EV Charger Rebates in 2026
lead: The federal credit for a home EV charger ended on June 30, 2026, and the Pennsylvania utilities whose rebate lists we could read have nothing for chargers. That is the honest answer. A home charger is still a good buy for many drivers, so here is how to price one and what to ask your utility.
cards_heading: What we checked for Pennsylvania EV chargers
cards_intro: Each card names the fact we keep on file, with the date we last read the official page.

cards.title: Federal 30C credit
cards.note: The credit was 30% of cost up to $1,000 per item for property placed in service at your main home through June 30, 2026. A charger installed later gets nothing.

cards.title: PPL Electric
cards.note: PPL's rebate catalog lists 15 items. None is a charger.

cards.title: PECO
cards.note: PECO's rebate page lists appliance, heating and cooling, new home, water heating and solar rebates. It lists no EV charger.

cards.title: Duquesne Light
cards.note: Its rebate store says rebates are not available yet while the next round is built. Ask whether chargers are included.

cards.title: Penelec and FirstEnergy
cards.note: Their pages would not load for us, so we show no amount.

after_cards: Utility pages change, and a charger offer can sit outside the main rebate list, for example in a separate time-of-use or EV program. We read only the rebate catalogs and indexes named above. Call your utility and ask about EV-specific offers before you buy.
sections: What the federal credit used to do

The IRS says the residential credit covered 30% of the cost of charging property placed in service at your main home between January 1, 2023 and June 30, 2026, up to $1,000 per item. If your charger went in on or before June 30, 2026 it may still count on your tax return, so ask your tax preparer. If it goes in after that date, there is no credit to claim.
Pricing an install without a rebate

Most home charging is a Level 2 charger on a 240-volt circuit, installed by a licensed electrician. Your costs are the charger, the circuit and the labour, and the circuit often costs more than the charger. A short run from the panel to a garage wall is the cheap case. A long run, a full panel or an older service can add real cost. Get at least two quotes, and ask each electrician to list the charger, the breaker, the wire and the labour on separate lines.

Before you buy a charger, ask the electrician whether your panel has room and whether your service is large enough. A panel that cannot take a new 240-volt circuit may need work first. Plug-in chargers that use an existing 240-volt outlet can avoid that cost, but the outlet and its wiring still need to be in good shape.

Charging at home is cheaper than fuel for most drivers, and some utilities offer lower rates at night. We did not verify any Pennsylvania time-of-use rate, so ask your utility if it has one, and compare it with your plain rate before you commit to a schedule.

A charger needs your landlord's approval if you rent, and a shared garage or a street space may not allow an install at all. Ask in writing before you pay for anything, and ask who will own the charger and the new circuit if you move.
claim_heading: What to do before you buy a home EV charger
claim_steps: Ask your electric utility whether it has any EV charger or EV rate offer.
Ask your tax preparer whether a charger installed by June 30, 2026 can still claim the federal credit.
Get two electrician quotes with separate lines for charger, breaker, wire and labour.
Check your panel capacity before you pick a charger.
Keep every receipt in case a program opens later.
links: what we could and could not confirm
faq: Is there a Pennsylvania rebate for a home EV charger?
None that we found. PPL's rebate catalog and PECO's rebate index list no charger, and we could not confirm Duquesne Light or FirstEnergy Pennsylvania.
Can I still claim the federal EV charger credit?
Only for a charger placed in service at your main home on or before June 30, 2026. The credit was 30% of cost up to $1,000 per item.
How much does a home charger install cost?
It depends on the electrician's quote. The circuit and labour can cost more than the charger itself, so get two quotes with each line listed.
Do I need a licensed electrician?
A Level 2 charger on a 240-volt circuit should be installed by a licensed electrician. Ask your township about permit rules.
Possibly. Keep your receipts and check your utility's rebate page. Pennsylvania's Penn Energy Savers program has not launched and its public pages do not mention chargers.
